units.translation: The punishing goddesses take pleasure in punishment, and the more barbaric and savage it is, the more so. A. had seen and heard enough of Persian penal justice. Immediately for ⟦1⟧ one compares ⟦2⟧; gouging out of eyes occurs ⟦3⟧ alongside other mutilations; castration of boys ⟦4⟧; stoning and a kind of crucifixion carried out on a Persian and his son by Xanthippos there 9, 120, ⟦5⟧ (189 f.) on 3000 Babylonians after the capture of Babylon 3, 159. In contrast to this, the Athenian, for whom only ⟦6⟧ and ⟦7⟧ were the punishments, had to feel humane and civilized. ⟦8⟧ like ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧; the word like ⟦11⟧ only here, but ⟦12⟧ in Rhesos 817 (⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧). Both adjectives belong to ⟦15⟧; standing by itself is ⟦16⟧ slaughterings, such as indeed also occurred in Hellas; then ⟦17⟧ (manuscript) ⟦18⟧ (boys) clearly for the thing; then ⟦19⟧ (as one must now write with Dindorf) ⟦20⟧. These too must be substantives, connected by ⟦21⟧, cf. 414 (also often elsewhere in A., though not in dialogue); the scholiast, who explains with ⟦22⟧ (⟦23⟧) ⟦24⟧ (⟦25⟧), strangely ignores the conjunction. From Herodian, however, in the scholia ⟦26⟧ is cited as an explanation for ⟦27⟧; better Bk. An. 372, 2 ⟦28⟧, ⟦29⟧, ⟦30⟧, ⟦31⟧ (Et. M. 53, 41; Hesych., s. ⟦32⟧). These meanings fit excellently and can be easily attached (except for ⟦33⟧) to ⟦34⟧, even if the manner of formation with -⟦35⟧ remains unclear. If, however, one accents -⟦36⟧, then ⟦37⟧, ⟦38⟧ are analogous, and the meaning is "where the extreme of evils is together." We are less well informed about ⟦39⟧, only that this word is grouped with ⟦40⟧ (⟦41⟧ ⟦42⟧) (⟦43⟧). The scholiast mixes in the Homeric (I 539) ⟦44⟧, which posed a great problem; after all, ⟦45⟧ does look like a feminine to ⟦46⟧ (⟦47⟧ – ⟦48⟧), and were it not for the ⟦49⟧, one could understand it with the scholia as an adjective (= ⟦50⟧) to ⟦51⟧.
